medicines.notes: Paracetamol; first-line simple analgesia for musculoskeletal injury (Therapeutic Guidelines: Pain)
Ibuprofen or naproxen; short course for soft tissue injury and fracture pain
Codeine or tramadol; added when simple analgesia is inadequate. Short course only per RACGP/PBS opioid stewardship
Oxycodone or tapentadol; reserved for severe injury, typically post-fracture or post-operative
Gastroprotection for the subset on NSAIDs with risk factors; not routine for short courses

Limb Injury.notes: Analgesia-only profile, stepped per Therapeutic Guidelines: Pain and RACGP acute pain guidance. Paracetamol and NSAIDs dominate; opioids are a minority short-course adjunct reflecting Australian opioid stewardship. No disease-modifying therapy applies to an acute injury.

Vaginal progesterone for threatened miscarriage, history of preterm birth, or short cervix
Alternative antiemetic for nausea/vomiting in pregnancy

Pregnancy.notes: Predominantly supplements (folic acid, iron, vitamins) with high uptake. Therapeutic drugs for specific indications. RANZCOG Antenatal Guidelines, NHMRC Iodine Supplementation 2010, PBS.
